questions.question: Figure 1 shows a linear relationship between log10 y (vertical axis) and log10 x (horizontal axis). The line passes through (0, 4) and (6, 0). Find an equation linking log10 y with log10 x.
steps: Intercept on the log10 y axis is 4.

questions.question: Figure 1 shows log10 y against log10 x through (0, 4) and (6, 0), with log10 y = 4 - (2/3) log10 x. Hence, or otherwise, express y in the form p x^q, where p and q are constants to be found.
steps: Take 10 to the power of both sides: y = 10^(4 - (2/3) log10 x).
Split the power: y = 10^4 x 10^(-(2/3) log10 x).

questions.question: Figure 3 shows the curve C1 with equation y = 5e^(x-1) + 3 and the curve C2 with equation y = 10 - x^2. The point P lies on C1 and has y coordinate 18. Find the x coordinate of P, writing your answer in the form ln k, where k is a constant to be found.
steps: x = 1 + ln 3 = ln e + ln 3 = ln(3e).

questions.question: C1 has equation y = 5e^(x-1) + 3 and C2 has equation y = 10 - x^2. The curves meet at x = alpha and x = beta. Using a suitable interval and a suitable function that should be stated, show that to 3 decimal places alpha = 1.134.
questions.answer: Using g(x) = 5e^(x-1) + x^2 - 7: g(1.1335) approx -0.0011 < 0 and g(1.1345) approx 0.0069 > 0, so alpha = 1.134 to 3 dp
steps: g is continuous and changes sign on [1.1335, 1.1345], so the root alpha lies in this interval.

questions.question: The iterative formula x(n+1) = -sqrt(7 - 5e^(x(n) - 1)) is used to find an approximation to beta. Using this formula with x1 = -3, find the value of x2 and the value of beta, giving each answer to 6 decimal places.
steps: The iteration converges quickly (derivative about 0.026), so beta approx -2.620330.

questions.question: The number of subscribers, N, to an online video streaming service is modelled by N = ab^t, where a and b are constants and t is the number of years since monitoring began. Figure 1 shows the line of log10 N against t through (0, 3.08) and (5, 3.85). Find an equation for this line.
steps: Intercept on the log10 N axis is 3.08.

questions.question: The number of subscribers N is modelled by N = ab^t, and log10 N = 0.154t + 3.08 from Figure 1. Find the value of a and the value of b, giving your answers to 3 significant figures.
steps: Taking log10: log10 N = log10 a + t log10 b.
Compare with log10 N = 0.154t + 3.08: log10 a = 3.08, so a = 10^3.08 approx 1202.
To 3 significant figures: a = 1.20 x 10^3 and b = 1.43.

questions.question: The number of subscribers N is modelled by N = ab^t with log10 N = 0.154t + 3.08. When t = T the number of subscribers is 500 000. According to the model, find the value of T.

The temperature theta degrees C inside an oven, t minutes after the oven is switched on, is given by theta = A - 180e^(-kt), where A and k are positive constants. The temperature inside the oven is initially 18 degrees C. Find the value of A.
steps: At t = 0, e^0 = 1, so theta = A - 180.

questions.question: The oven model is theta = 198 - 180e^(-kt). At t = 5 the temperature is 90 degrees C. Show that k = p ln q, where p and q are rational numbers to be found.
steps: So p = 1/5 and q = 5/3, both rational.

questions.question: Using theta = 198 - 180e^(-kt) with k = (1/5) ln(5/3), find the temperature inside the oven 9 minutes after the oven is switched on, giving your answer to 3 significant figures.

The oven temperature is theta = 198 - 180e^(-kt) with k = (1/5) ln(5/3). Find the rate of increase of the temperature 9 minutes after the oven is switched on, giving your answer in degrees C per minute to 3 significant figures.
steps: The temperature is increasing at about 7.33 degrees C per minute.

questions.question: The total mass of gold G tonnes extracted from a mine is modelled by G = 40 - 30e^(1-0.05t), t >= k, G >= 0, where t is the number of years after 1st January 1800 (the exponent is read as e^(1-0.05t) from the scan). (i) Find the value of k. (ii) Hence find the year and month in which gold started being extracted from the mine. (Parts (i) and (ii) share one mark allocation of 3.)
steps: 14.246 years after 1 Jan 1800 is 1814 plus 0.246 of a year (about 90 days).
This is about 31 March 1814, so March 1814.

questions.question: The gold mass model is G = 40 - 30e^(1-0.05t), t >= k. Find the total mass of gold extracted from the mine up to 1st January 1870.
steps: 1st January 1870 is t = 70 years after 1st January 1800.
The total mass is approximately 37.5 tonnes.

questions.question: The gold mass model is G = 40 - 30e^(1-0.05t), t >= k, G >= 0. There is a limit to the mass of gold that can be extracted. State the value of this limit.
steps: As t tends to infinity, -0.05t tends to -infinity, so e^(1-0.05t) tends to 0.

questions.question: Figure 1 shows the line l, a linear relationship between log10 y and x. The line passes through (0, 1.5) and (-4.8, 0). Write down an equation for l.
steps: Intercept on the log10 y axis is 1.5.

questions.question: The line l shows log10 y against x through (0, 1.5) and (-4.8, 0). Hence, or otherwise, express y in the form k b^x, giving the values of the constants k and b to 3 significant figures.
steps: Take 10 to the power of both sides: y = 10^(1.5 + (5/16)x).
So k = 10^1.5 approx 31.6 and b = 10^0.3125 approx 2.05.
To 3 significant figures: k = 31.6 and b = 2.05.

questions.question: Figure 2 shows a sketch of the curve y = |2 - 4ln(x + 1)| for x > k, where k is a constant. The curve has an asymptote at x = k, cuts the y axis at A and meets the x axis at B. State the value of k.
steps: The modulus grows without bound when ln(x + 1) tends to -infinity.
This happens when x + 1 tends to 0, so x tends to -1.
So the asymptote is x = -1 and k = -1.

questions.question: The curve y = |2 - 4ln(x + 1)| meets the y axis at A and the x axis at B, as in Figure 2. (i) Find the y coordinate of A. (ii) Find the exact x coordinate of B. (Parts (i) and (ii) share one mark allocation of 3.)
questions.answer: (i) A = (0, 2), so y = 2; (ii) B has x = sqrt(e) - 1

questions.question: Using algebra and showing your working, find the set of values of x such that |2 - 4ln(x + 1)| > 3, for x > -1.

The amount of antibiotic x milligrams in a patient's bloodstream t hours after a dose satisfies log10 x = 2.74 - 0.079t. Show that this can be written as x = p q^(-t), where p and q are constants. Give p to the nearest whole number and q to 2 significant figures.
questions.answer: p = 550 (549.5 to nearest whole number), q = 1.2
steps: Take 10 to the power of both sides: x = 10^(2.74 - 0.079t).
p = 10^2.74 approx 549.5, which is 550 to the nearest whole number.

questions.question: With reference to the equation x = p q^(-t) in part (a), interpret the value of the constant p.
questions.answer: p is the amount of antibiotic in the bloodstream at t = 0, i.e. immediately after the dose (about 550 mg)
steps: At t = 0, q^0 = 1, so x = p.
So p is the amount of antibiotic in the bloodstream when t = 0, just after the dose is given.

questions.question: A different dose gives x = 400 x 1.4^(-t) where x milligrams and t hours. Use calculus to find, to 2 significant figures, the value of dx/dt when t = 5.
steps: To 2 significant figures: dx/dt approx -25 mg per hour.

questions.question: The number of fruit flies F in a population t days after the start of a study is modelled by F = 350e^(kt)/(9 + e^(kt)), where k is a constant. Find the number of fruit flies in the population at the start of the study.
Fruit fly model F = 350e^(kt)/(9 + e^(kt)). Given that there are 200 fruit flies 15 days after the start, show that k = (1/15) ln 12.
Fruit fly model F = 350e^(kt)/(9 + e^(kt)) with k = (1/15) ln 12. When t = T the population is increasing at 10 per day. Find the possible values of T, giving your answers to one decimal place.
questions.answer: T approx 5.7 or T approx 20.8 days
steps: Let E = e^(kT). Set 3150k E/(9 + E)^2 = 10 with 3150k = 210 ln 12 approx 521.63.
T = ln E / k with k approx 0.165661: T approx 20.8 or T approx 5.7 days.

questions.question: The functions f: x -> e^x + 2, x real, and g: x -> ln x, x > 0, are defined. State the range of f.
The functions f: x -> e^x + 2 (x real) and g: x -> ln x (x > 0) are defined. Find fg(x), giving your answer in its simplest form.
The function f: x -> e^x + 2 (x real). Find the exact value of x for which f(2x + 3) = 6.
The function f: x -> e^x + 2 (x real). Find f^-1, stating its domain.
steps: Let y = e^x + 2, so e^x = y - 2.
The domain of f^-1 is the range of f, so x > 2.

questions.question: The functions f: x -> e^x + 2 (x real) and g: x -> ln x (x > 0) are defined. On the same axes sketch the curves with equations y = f(x) and y = f^-1(x), giving the coordinates of all the points where the curves cross the axes.
questions.answer: y = f(x) crosses the y axis at (0, 3) with no x intercept (asymptote y = 2); y = f^-1(x) crosses the x axis at (3, 0) with no y intercept (asymptote x = 2)
steps: y = f(x) = e^x + 2 has horizontal asymptote y = 2 and never meets the x axis.
Put x = 0: f(0) = 3, so it crosses the y axis at (0, 3).
y = f^-1(x) = ln(x - 2) has vertical asymptote x = 2 and does not meet the y axis.
Put y = 0: x - 2 = 1, so it crosses the x axis at (3, 0).
The two curves are reflections of each other in the line y = x.

questions.question: The functions f(x) = 12/(x + 1) (x > 0) and g(x) = (5/2) ln x (x > 0) are defined. Find, in simplest form, the value of fg(e^2).
The function f(x) = 12/(x + 1), x > 0, x real. Find f^-1.
steps: The range of f for x > 0 is 0 < f(x) < 12, so the domain of f^-1 is 0 < x < 12.

questions.question: The functions f(x) = 12/(x + 1) (x > 0) and g(x) = (5/2) ln x (x > 0) are defined. Hence, or otherwise, find all real solutions of the equation f^-1(x) = f(x).
steps: f(x) is only defined for x > 0, so x = -4 is rejected.
Check x = 3: f^-1(3) = 3 and f(3) = 3, so x = 3.

questions.topic: Log Linear Equation And Exact Value
questions.question: Figure 1 shows the linear relationship between log6 T (vertical) and log6 x (horizontal), passing through (0, 4) and (2, 0). (i) Find an equation linking log6 T and log6 x. (ii) Hence find the exact value of T when x = 216. (Parts (i) and (ii) share one mark allocation of 3.)
questions.answer: (i) log6 T = 4 - 2 log6 x; (ii) T = 1/36 when x = 216

questions.question: Using the line in Figure 1 with log6 T = 4 - 2 log6 x, find an equation, not involving logs, linking T with x.

Microbes: N = aT^b, where a and b are constants and T is the number of days after the start of the experiment. Show that this relationship can be expressed as log10 N = m log10 T + c, giving m and c in terms of a and/or b.
questions.answer: m = b and c = log10 a
steps: Take log10 of both sides: log10 N = log10 a + b log10 T.
This has the form log10 N = m log10 T + c.
So m = b and c = log10 a.

questions.question: Figure 2 shows the line of best fit for values of log10 N plotted against log10 T. Use the information provided to estimate the number of microbes present in the culture 3 days after the start of the experiment.
questions.answer: approx 940 microbes (estimate from the line: intercept about 1.9, gradient about 2.25)
steps: Read the line from Figure 2: it meets the log10 N axis at about 1.9 and passes through about (1.0, 4.15) and (1.2, 4.5).
Gradient m = (4.15 - 1.9)/1.0 approx 2.25, so log10 N approx 2.25 log10 T + 1.9.
At T = 3: log10 T = 0.4771, so log10 N approx 2.25 x 0.4771 + 1.9 approx 2.9735.
N approx 10^2.9735 approx 940, so about 940 microbes (estimate from the graph).

questions.question: With reference to the model N = aT^b, interpret the value of the constant a.
questions.answer: a is the number of microbes present when T = 1 (after 1 day), approx 10^1.9 = 79
steps: When T = 1, T^b = 1, so N = a.
a is therefore the number of microbes in the culture after 1 day.

questions.question: The amount of antibiotic in the bloodstream is modelled by x = De^(-0.2t), where x mg is the amount, D mg the dose and t hours the time after the dose. A first dose of 15 mg is given. Use the model to find the amount of antibiotic in the bloodstream 4 hours after the dose is given, in mg to 3 decimal places.
steps: So x = 6.740 mg to 3 decimal places.

questions.question: A first dose of 15 mg is given. A second dose of 15 mg is given 5 hours after the first. Using the same model, show that the total amount of antibiotic 2 hours after the second dose is given is 13.754 mg to 3 decimal places.
steps: The first dose is then 7 hours old: 15e^(-0.2 x 7) = 15e^(-1.4) approx 3.69896.
The second dose is 2 hours old: 15e^(-0.2 x 2) = 15e^(-0.4) approx 10.05481.
So the total is 13.754 mg to 3 decimal places.

questions.question: No more doses are given. At time T hours after the second dose the total amount of antibiotic is 7.5 mg. Show that T = a ln(b + b/e), where a and b are integers to be determined.
questions.answer: a = 5, b = 2, so T = 5 ln(2 + 2/e) approx 5.03 hours
steps: The first dose is then T + 5 hours old and the second dose is T hours old.

questions.question: The area N mm^2 of a dish covered by bacteria, t days after monitoring began (0 <= t <= 30), is modelled by log10 N = 0.0646t + 1.478. Show that this may be written as N = ab^t, where a and b are constants to be found. Give a to the nearest integer and b to 3 significant figures.
steps: Take 10 to the power of both sides: N = 10^(1.478) x 10^(0.0646t).
So a = 10^1.478 approx 30.06, which is 30 to the nearest integer.
b = 10^0.0646 approx 1.16038, which is 1.16 to 3 significant figures.

questions.question: The bacteria area model is log10 N = 0.0646t + 1.478, 0 <= t <= 30. Use the model to find the area of the dish covered by bacteria 30 days after monitoring began, in mm^2 to 2 significant figures.
steps: To 2 significant figures: N approx 2600 mm^2.

questions.question: The percentage P of the population of a small country with access to the internet is modelled by P = ab^t, where t is the number of years after the start of 2005. A graph of log10 P against t has an approximately straight line with gradient 0.09 and intercept 0.68 on the log10 P axis. Find the value of a and the value of b, giving your answers to 2 decimal places.
steps: log10 P = log10 a + t log10 b, so the intercept gives log10 a = 0.68.
a = 10^0.68 approx 4.786, which is 4.79 to 2 decimal places.
The gradient gives log10 b = 0.09, so b = 10^0.09 approx 1.2303, which is 1.23 to 2 decimal places.

questions.question: In the context of the model P = ab^t for internet access, give a practical interpretation of the constant a.
questions.answer: a is the percentage of the population with internet access at the start of 2005 (t = 0), approx 4.79%
steps: At t = 0, b^0 = 1, so P = a.
t = 0 is the start of 2005, so a is the percentage with internet access at that time.

questions.question: Using the internet access model P = ab^t with a = 4.79 and b = 1.23 (t years after the start of 2005), estimate the percentage of the population with access to the internet at the start of 2015.
steps: P = 10^1.58 approx 38.0, so about 38.0% of the population.

questions.question: The number of toads N in a population t years after the start of a study is modelled by N = 900e^(0.12t)/(2e^(0.12t) + 1), t >= 0. According to this model, calculate the number of toads in the population at the start of the study.
The toad model is N = 900e^(0.12t)/(2e^(0.12t) + 1). Find the value of t when there are 420 toads in the population, giving your answer to 2 decimal places.
steps: t approx 16.22 years to 2 decimal places.

questions.question: The toad model is N = 900e^(0.12t)/(2e^(0.12t) + 1), t >= 0. Explain why, according to this model, the number of toads in the population can never reach 500.
questions.answer: N = 450 - 450/(2e^(0.12t) + 1) is always less than 450, so N can never reach 500
steps: Divide top and bottom by 2 to write N = 450 x 2E/(2E + 1), where E = e^(0.12t).
Since E > 0, 450/(2E + 1) > 0, so N < 450 for all t.
As t tends to infinity N tends to 450, which is below 500, so N never reaches 500.
